title: Agent Tool Calling: Function Calling, the Agent Loop and Safe Permissions
summary: Quick revision notes on how LLM agents call tools via JSON schemas, run the observe-think-act loop, feed tool results back into context, use ReAct and planning, stop safely, and restrict tool permissions.

chapters.title: Function Calling and the Agent Mental Model
points: Function calling: you describe tools (name, description, JSON Schema for parameters) and the model returns a structured tool call; the model never executes anything, your code does
A tool definition has three parts: name, description (the model's main cue for when to use it), and input_schema (JSON Schema with type object, properties, required)
Tool call output is a block like {type: tool_use, id, name, input}; stop_reason is tool_use when the model wants a tool run
Chatbot vs agent: a chatbot answers in one model call; an agent loops, calling tools and reading results until the task is done
Schema tip: use enums, descriptions per property and required lists to constrain arguments; vague schemas produce wrong or missing arguments

chapters.title: The Agent Loop: Observe, Think, Act
points: Loop: observe (messages plus latest tool results) → think (model decides next step) → act (emit tool call) → repeat until the model answers without a tool call
Pseudocode: while True: resp = model(messages, tools); if resp.stop_reason != tool_use: break; run each tool; append results; continue
The assistant message containing tool_use must be appended to history before the tool_result message, or the API rejects the turn
Each tool_result must carry the matching tool_use_id; with parallel tool calls, return all results together in one user message
The model is stateless: the full growing message list is resent every iteration, so context and cost grow per step

chapters.title: Tool Results Back into Context
points: Tool result goes back as a user-role tool_result block with the tool_use_id and content (text or JSON string)
Report failures as results with is_error true and a useful message so the model can retry or change approach, instead of crashing the loop
Truncate, paginate or summarize large outputs; dumping a 50k-token response bloats context and degrades reasoning
Return only fields the model needs; unfiltered API payloads waste tokens and may leak secrets
Treat tool output as untrusted data: web pages or files can contain prompt injection text that tries to give the model new instructions

chapters.title: ReAct and Planning
points: ReAct = Reason + Act: interleave a thought, an action (tool call) and an observation, then repeat; reasoning is grounded by real observations
Trace shape: Thought: need the user's order status → Action: get_order(id=42) → Observation: shipped → Thought: enough, answer
Plan-and-execute: write the full step list up front, then run steps; cheaper and more predictable, but brittle if early steps change the situation
ReAct vs plan-and-execute: ReAct adapts step by step but can wander and costs more calls; planning is structured but needs re-planning on failure
Hybrid in practice: draft a short plan, execute with ReAct, and re-plan when an observation contradicts the plan

chapters.title: Stopping Conditions and Tool Permission Safety
points: Natural stop: model replies with no tool call (stop_reason end_turn); never rely on it alone
Hard guards: max iterations (e.g. 10-25), token or cost budget, wall-clock timeout; on hit, return a partial result with an explanation
Detect loops: same tool with same arguments repeated, or no progress across steps; break out or ask for help
Least privilege: give each agent only the tools it needs, read-only by default, scoped credentials, allowlist not denylist
Human approval gate for irreversible or high-impact actions (delete, send, pay, deploy); validate arguments against the schema server-side and sandbox code execution

chapters.title: Agent Tool Calling Cheat Sheet
points: Flow: define tools → send messages plus tools → stop_reason tool_use → run tool → append assistant turn and tool_result → loop until end_turn
Tool def: name, description, input_schema {type: object, properties, required}
Result block: {type: tool_result, tool_use_id, content, is_error}
Guards: max steps, budget, timeout, repeat-call detection
Safety: least privilege, allowlist, approval for destructive actions, treat tool output as untrusted
